sanskrit: aghamāram aghaśaṃsaṃ nirṛthaṃ durhārde dantaṃ pra hiṇomi ghoram | so asyāttu dvipadaś catuṣpadaḥ śivo asmabhyaṃ sumanā astv eṣaḥ ||
english: I drive forth the terrible tooth — the death-bringer, the evil-speaker, the worthless, the hard-to-ward-off, the fierce one. Let it devour his two-footed and four-footed ones; yet may it be auspicious to us, well-disposed.

sanskrit: śivaṃ te dantaṃ haviṣā kṛṇomi śivo mahyaṃ kurvate danto astu | śivāni te trīṇi trikadrukāṇi santu śivo mahyaṃ nabhasī rodasī stām ||
english: With oblation I make your tooth auspicious; may the tooth become auspicious for me who render it so. May your three Trikadruka rites be auspicious; may the two heavenly vaults — sky and earth — be auspicious for me.

sanskrit: pururūpā pṛthupeśā araṃkṛd vahator asi | pratiṣṭhāsi catuṣpadāṃ yas ta eṣa pañcamaḥ pādas taṃ tena prati gṛhṇāmi ||
english: You are of many forms, broadly ornamented, self-sufficient, a bearer. You are the foundation of four-footed creatures; this fifth foot that is yours — with it I take hold of that one in return.

sanskrit: sasarparīr amatiṃ bādhamānā bṛhan mimāya jamadagnidattā | ā sūryasya duhitā tatāna śravo deveṣv amṛtam ajuryam ||
english: The Sasarparī, driving away ignorance, sounded loud — given by Jamadagni. The daughter of the Sun spread renown immortal and undecaying among the gods.

sanskrit: sasarparīr abharat tūyam ebhyo 'dhi śravaḥ pāñcajanyāsu kṛṣṭiṣu | sā pakṣyā navyamāyur dadhānā yāṃ me pulasti jamadagnayo daduḥ ||
english: The Sasarparī quickly brought glory over these five peoples. She, wing-bearing, bestowing fresh life — her whom Pulastī and the Jamadagnis gave to me.

sanskrit: aghnye dūramūt kanda ni padaś caturo jahi | adhā goduhaḥ śīrṣaṇi śaphām̐ urasi vādaya ||
english: O inviolable cow, driving far away, strike down the four feet of the one who kicks. Then on the head of the milk-thief let the hooves resound upon his chest.

sanskrit: śṛṅgābhyām upa sraṣṭāraṃ padāvartaya goduham | atho ye anye tiṣṭhanti tān viṣūco vi nāśaya ||
english: With your horns knock over the milk-thief; with your foot trample him down. And those others who stand by — scatter and destroy them in all directions.

sanskrit: yathā nartā sakṣikājiṃ ni kulpham abhinṛtyati | evā tvam aghnye padaḥ sarvān sākam ud ardaya ||
english: Just as a dancer treads down with her anklet in a contest-dance, so, O inviolable cow, stir up all those feet together.

sanskrit: ud u kṣīram uttabhitaṃ syandantām asya dhenavaḥ | asṛk tasya gāvo duhrāṃ yo asmān nāpacāyati ||
english: Let the milk be raised up and let his cows flow freely. Let the cows yield blood for him who does not honor us.

sanskrit: ṛkṣīkāyā yathā mano vyāghrasya yathā manaḥ | evā tasya gavāṃ mano yo asmān nāpacāyati ||
english: As is the mind of the she-bear, as is the mind of the tiger — so be the mind of the cows of him who does not honor us.

sanskrit: uttamosy oṣadhīnāṃ vīrudhāṃ balavattamaḥ | sasyandana tvam oṣadhe sarvāḥ syandaya gā imāḥ ||
english: You are the highest of herbs, the most powerful of plants. O herb Sasyandana, make all these cows flow with milk.

sanskrit: aranturathantu | vaneṣu śuṣmo astu te pṛthivyām astu yad dharaḥ ||
english: Let them run, let them roll about. In the forests let your vigor be; on the earth let that which is yellow be.

sanskrit: akṛd aśvo akṛt kharo akṛd aśvataro hariḥ | evāsi bahvaghe tava bhasan nadatv āsicā ||
english: The horse has done it, the donkey has done it, the yellow mule has done it. So too you, O greatly fierce one — let your vagina cry out with the ladle-pouring.

sanskrit: yathā nadati gardabha evā nadati te bhasat | vrīher yavasya māṣasy- -aitat paśyābhidarśanam ||
english: As the donkey brays, so your vagina brays. Of rice, of barley, of beans — behold this manifest demonstration.

sanskrit: ud bhare dyāvāpṛthivī ud āpa ud agnim ud indram ut sūryam ud rātrim ud ahaḥ ||
english: I lift up heaven and earth, I lift up the waters, I lift up fire, I lift up Indra, I lift up the sun, I lift up night, I lift up day.

sanskrit: namaskṛtya dyāvāpṛthivībhyām antarikṣāya mṛtyave | mekṣyāmy ūrdhvas tiṣṭhan mā mā hiṃsiṣur īśvarāḥ ||
english: Having paid homage to heaven and earth, to the atmosphere, to death — standing upright I shall stir; let the lords not harm me.

sanskrit: yan meḍhvā yad apsarasaḥ payo devīr ahṛṣata | tad ihopa hṛyāmahe cakṣuṣe ca balāya ca | devānāṃ devahūtyā mayi tyā devatāḥ punaḥ ||
english: Whatever vital sap the divine Apsarases stole away through their fornication — that we bring back here for sight and for strength. Through the invocation of the gods, may those deities return to me.

sanskrit: yāsya doṣā rasasya me tvaṃ devi tatarpitha | nārāśaṃsena stomen- -āhaṃ tvat punar ā dade yuṣmad apsarasas pari ||
english: O goddess, you who satisfied yourself with the vital sap of my arm-strength — with the hymn of Nārāśaṃsa I take it back from you; I take it back from you Apsarases.

sanskrit: yan me tanvo rasaṃ vayam ud apsarasas pari | nārāśaṃsena stomena prajām ā pyāyāmahe ||
english: The vital sap of our bodies which we take back from the Apsarases — with the hymn of Nārāśaṃsa we swell our progeny.

sanskrit: yan me payo viṣiṣice jāgrataḥ svapataś ca yat | punas tad adya me devā ā siñcantu tanū adhi ||
english: Whatever sap of mine has been drained away — both while I was waking and while I was sleeping — let the gods today pour that back upon my body.

sanskrit: yad adya dugdhaṃ pṛthivīm asakta yad oṣadhīr vyasarad yad āpaḥ | vatse payo gavi payo yad asyām asmāṃs tat sacatāṃ payaḥ ||
english: What was milked today and clung to the earth, what flowed into the herbs and into the waters — the milk in the calf, the milk in the cow, whatever milk is in her — let that milk accompany us.

sanskrit: parā patanty āśavo 'śvā adhodhuraṃ yathā | evā mūtra pra bhidyasva vi vaster āsyaṃ sṛja ||
english: As swift horses fly forward, pulling the yoke downward — so, urine, burst forth; open wide the mouth of the bladder and release it.

sanskrit: viṣitaṃ te vastibilam ity ekā ||
english: "The orifice of your bladder is opened" — so runs one verse.

sanskrit: asya pāre samudrasya śukraṃ jyotir amartyam | tan naḥ pātv aṃhasas tan naḥ pātu viśvataḥ ||
english: On the far shore of this ocean shines bright, immortal light. May that protect us from distress; may that protect us from all sides.

sanskrit: ā no medhā sumatir viśvarūpā hiraṇyavarṇā jagatī jagamyāt | sā no agne medhā juṣatām iha pracetāḥ ||
english: May wisdom, good favor, of all forms, golden-hued, mobile and approachable, come to us. O Agni, O Pracetas, may that wisdom delight in us here.

sanskrit: niṣ krāmatv iṣiryo atra praviṣṭo vayāṣṭhaś ca sayujā yāv iha staḥ | sapta ṛṣīṇāṃ syūmaraśmiḥ pathaitu svān mṛgān punar apy etu kṛṣṇaḥ ||
english: Let the vigorous one who has entered here go forth, and likewise the pair — the bird-percher and his consort — who are here together. Let Syūmaraśmi go on the path of the seven seers; let Kṛṣṇa return again to his own wild creatures.

sanskrit: sapta ṛṣīn gaccha syūmaraśmaye mṛgān kṛṣṇaḥ sacatāṃ vājo aśvam | īḍo asmān suprajasaḥ suvīrān saha yajñena payasā sacātai ||
english: Go to the seven seers, O Syūmaraśmi; let Kṛṣṇa accompany the wild creatures; let the prize accompany the horse. Let the praiseworthy one accompany us — us with good offspring and good heroes — together with the sacrifice and with milk.

sanskrit: namo astv ṛṣaye syūmaraśmaye namaḥ kṛṣṇāyota yo vājo asya | namo devāyārvateṣu jiṣṇave 'yaṃ no vājī pra tirāty āyuḥ ||
english: Homage be to the seer Syūmaraśmi; homage to Kṛṣṇa and to the prize that is his. Homage to the divine victor among swift horses — may this prize-winning steed extend our life.

sanskrit: ati yanty ahāny ati rātrīr aty uṣasaḥ | āpo antardhāvarīs tābhir antar dadhe tvā ||
english: The days pass by, the nights pass by, the dawns pass by. The waters that run within the hidden channels — with those I place you within.

sanskrit: yathā naidāghye māsi bahvīḥ śuṣyanty oṣadhīḥ | evā pra śuṣya mām anu yac ca paśyāmi yac ca na ||
english: Just as in the summer month many herbs dry up — so dry up following me, both what I see and what I do not see.

sanskrit: pāṭā bibharty aṅkuśaṃ hiraṇyavantam aṅkinam | tenāham anyeṣāṃ striya ā lumpāmi mamed asan ||
english: The Pāṭā plant bears a hook, golden and marked. With it I seize away the women of others — may they be mine.
